transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey Dr. [Name]. Yeah, so... I guess I'm here because work is just getting really out of hand lately. I'm a construction manager, and, well, I'll start a safety briefing for the guys, or I'll sit down in the trailer to do a plan review, and I am honestly trying so hard to just pay attention to the paper in front of me. 

But within minutes, my mind is completely off on like three other job problems. Like Tuesday, the drywall supplier shorted us two pallets, and I had to get on the phone with the rep—this guy named Gary. Nice enough guy, but he always messes up the delivery manifests. I swear he does it on purpose to save on freight costs, because last month he did the exact same thing with the exterior sheathing... 

Anyway, sorry, what was I saying? Right, the plans. Because my head is always spinning off on stuff like Gary and the drywall, I end up completely missing things in these safety reviews and blueprints that I know for a fact I should have caught. It's just getting really frustrating.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility and trouble focusing since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started or worsened recently?

Oh, no, it's been forever. Like, back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat. I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework... man, I remember losing this one specific homework folder. It was bright red, had a massive monster truck on it. Bigfoot, I think? 

Yeah, my dad took me to see Bigfoot at the arena when I was maybe seven or eight. Loudest thing I've ever heard in my life. We had these cheap foam earplugs that kept falling out, and we bought these stadium nachos that were basically just liquid plastic cheese. I actually spilled that cheese all over the backseat of my dad's Chevy on the ride home, and he was so mad because he had just detailed it. He loved that truck. Kept it running for like two hundred thousand miles before the transmission finally gave out on a trip up to the lake... 

Wait, why am I talking about the Chevy? I'm sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, right, school. Yeah, so the teachers also said I always rushed through directions before I actually understood them. Just flew right through the assignments to get them over with. So, yeah, it's definitely been going on a long time.

Aside from the trouble focusing, do you notice yourself feeling physically restless, fidgeting, or acting or speaking impulsively—like interrupting others or making snap decisions—either now or when you were a kid?

Yeah, physically restless, for sure. Even now. Like, in meetings where everybody else can just sit through the whole thing, I’m always the guy standing up, walking to the coffee machine, stepping outside to check something, or just making some excuse to move around. I can't stand sitting still. The coffee on the site is terrible, by the way. It’s this cheap bulk stuff the general contractor buys, tastes like burnt dirt. My wife bought me this really nice French press for my birthday last year, one of those insulated stainless steel ones, but I left it in my truck and someone smashed the window and stole it while I was parked at a diner. Can you believe that? Over a coffee maker. I had to pay a three hundred dollar deductible for the window, which is ridiculous because the glass itself is only like... wait, what was I saying? Right, yeah, I'm always up and moving around during meetings. Can't stay in my seat.
